lessons.headline: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization

sourceLinks.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization

summaryBullets: Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) aligns a language model to a general preference function by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player preference game.

Its practical variant, DNO-Prct, iterates on-policy sampling, LLM-based rating of the samples together with a teacher's gold response, large-margin preference-pair selection and a DPO-style contrastive update.

We re-implement DNO-Prct independently and study it on two open-weight instruct models, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1, with GPT-4o or a larger open-weight model of the same family as the annotator.

lessons.headline: I removed 85% of gemma's weights (and it is mostly fine)

sourceLinks.title: I removed 85% of gemma's weights (and it is mostly fine)

summaryBullets: I pruned Gemma 4 26B-A4B, an MoE model, down to 15% of its original size, and the model still does great on one narrow task.
It gets 92% agreement with the original on a classification task.
That’s close to how often the 12B agrees with the 26B on the same ticks, which is 90%.
